subject: MAP: Request for Close-Date Containment Plan & Exec Clearance
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@acme.io>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP review — procurement timing concern

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks again for the MAP walkthrough yesterday. Two quick updates from procurement that will affect the close timeline: they just flagged a mandatory vendor security addendum and an internal renewal window that requires legal review before awards that is likely to add 5–7 business days.

We’re committed to closing in September but procurement is asking for a containment plan that shows: a) the minimum scope Acme must validate to go-live, b) fallback options if the legal approval pushes beyond the end of the month, and c) an exec-level clearance path if procurement needs to extend.

I attached the latest MAP (acme_map_v2.xlsx) with the sections they highlighted. Can you share a short containment plan + quick decision matrix by EOD Monday? If needed, we can escalate internally from our side to speed legal.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick sync if that helps.

Best,
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Programs
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_map_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP review — procurement timing concern

Sara —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the MAP export. We can do that. High level options we should prepare (I’ll own a short containment plan + matrix):

- Option A (Containment): Prioritize a 2-day eval for the essential feature set (auth, inference, telemetry). Target go/no-go demo to procurement reviewers so they can validate immediate business value.
- Option B (Staggered go-live): Ship with hosted API for production traffic while enabling Private (VPC) fallback if procurement requires additional contractual controls — reduces legal risk window.
- Option C (Escalate): If legal approval is the only blocker, we escalate for exec clearance and propose a short-term invoice hold rather than full delay.

Can the procurement team confirm which of the following they prefer: 
  1) Minimal acceptance scope (list) — fastest route,
  2) Must-have contractual controls (specific clauses), or
  3) Exec escalation route (names and timeline)?

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll draft a 1‑page containment plan + decision matrix and share by COB Monday. (attachment: proposed_timeline_v3.png)
- Priyom — can you start a scoped MAP re-baseline and flag any eval items that can be deferred?
- Neha — can you confirm the security artifacts we can produce immediately for procurement (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)?

If helpful, let’s lock a 30-minute sync early Monday to run through the containment plan and any procurement asks.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_timeline_v3.png (PNG)

Subject: Re: MAP: Request for Close-Date Containment Plan & Exec Clearance

All —

Good call from Sara. A couple of practical items from CSM side that will help procurement feel comfortable without delaying close:
- Prepare a short acceptance checklist (3–5 items) that procurement can sign off on after the demo.
- Offer a 30-day production support window with proactive monitoring and a named TAM — reduces risk perception.
- Provide a runbook excerpt showing rollback and data retention controls.

Neha — can you confirm whether the SOC 2 letter + audit summary is sufficient, or do they want underlying logs exported? If they want logs we’ll need to confirm retention windows.

I’ll draft the acceptance checklist template and the TAM commitment language; will share a draft in the morning.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara@acme.io>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Request for Close-Date Containment Plan & Exec Clearance

Team / Sara —

Security update and options for procurement:

1) Immediate artifacts we can hand to procurement (same-day):
   - SOC 2 Type II report (summary),
   - Security whitepaper + architecture diagram,
   - KMS & key rotation policy summary.

2) Medium-term (3–5 business days):
   - Exportable audit logs for the eval window (can confirm retention),
   - Contract language for data residency/KMS binding if Acme requires.

3) Fallback that short-circuits the legal ask:
   - Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed keys — this avoids some addendum requirements. If procurement would accept this as a condition, we can commit to a short-term private instance while legal finishes the vendor addendum.

I’m attaching a draft internal risk log (summary) and will convert to the external-facing risk register for Acme. Priyom — please start the re-baseline of the MAP; call out which eval tests we can table and which we cannot.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_risk_log_draft.pdf (internal)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: ACTION: MAP containment plan + exec clearance request (final)

Sara / Procurement / Team —

Per our threads and internal reviews, attached is the consolidated containment plan and a concise risk register for Acme (redwood_risk_log_20250915.pdf). Summary and ask below.

Executive summary (short):
- Root cause: Procurement requires a vendor addendum that introduces a 5–7 business day legal review window; this creates a high risk of moving our target close beyond Sep 30.
- Containment approach: Prioritize an essential acceptance scope to allow a limited production kickoff (hosted) while offering a Private fallback (VPC + CMK) if procurement insists on contractual controls.
- Decision matrix: If procurement can accept the Private fallback OR sign the acceptance checklist post-demo, we proceed without changing the target close. If not, we request a formal exec clearance to extend close by up to 7 business days.

Concrete asks (procurement):
1) Confirm by EOD Tuesday whether Acme will accept the Private fallback as an interim control OR confirm the specific contractual language required.
2) If procurement needs an extension, please provide the name(s) and availability of the exec approver(s) so we can escalate with a proposed SOW amendment and short-term invoice hold.

Internal action owners (brief):
- Jonas: coordinate exec escalation and draft SOW amendment if needed.
- Laura: finalize the 3-item acceptance checklist and TAM commitment (deliver by tomorrow morning).
- Priyom: finalize the MAP re-baseline with deferred eval items (deliverable: MAP_v2_rebaseline.xlsx).
- Neha: publish the external risk register and SOC 2 artifacts to procurement (done by EOD Monday).

I’ve attached the consolidated risk register for Acme and a one‑pager containment timeline. If procurement confirms Private fallback, we will not change the public close date. If procurement cannot accept fallback or sign the checklist, please indicate exec approver contact info and we’ll initiate escalation immediately.

Thanks — ready to jump on a call if you want to run through the decision matrix.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_risk_log_20250915.pdf (PDF)
